transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, I just... I really need to figure out what's going on with me because it's getting incredibly frustrating. The main thing, and I guess the reason
Have you been feeling down or depressed a lot lately?
No, not really. I mean, um, I wouldn't say depressed. It's more just... frustration? Like, my mom actually asks me that sometimes, she always asks if
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when you don’t want to?
Worrying? Um... no, not really. I mean, my mom worries enough for the both of us, honestly. She's always like, 'Aren't you worried about this
Do you often have trouble paying attention, even when you want to focus?
Yes! Exactly. That is exactly it. It's like... I really want to focus, I do. Like, take the other day, for example. I was sitting down at my desk,
Did you have trouble paying attention as a child?

Oh, yeah. Definitely. It's not just a new thing. I mean, my mom could probably write a whole book about it. Even way back in elementary school, it was a whole thing. Like, I remember being in third grade, Mrs. Peterson's class, and she was always, always moving my seat. I think I sat next to every single kid in that room at some point because she was trying to find a spot where I wouldn't distract anyone. Because I was always talking out of turn, just blurting things out when I thought of them, you know? And the homework... man, I'd either forget to do it, or I'd do it and leave it on the kitchen counter, or I'd just lose it in my backpack which was basically a black hole. And when we had those worksheets in class, I'd just want to be done with them so I could do something else, so I'd rush through them as fast as humanly possible, and they'd be full of all these stupid, careless mistakes. My mom would get so mad when she saw the red marks, but I just... I couldn't slow down enough to check my work, it was like my brain was already on the next thing before my pencil even finished the sentence.
